chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, who said:
One of our companions asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام and said: May I be made your ransom, a man sleeps with another man under one blanket.

He said: “Is he a relative by kinship?” He said: No. He said: “Is it out of necessity?” He said: No. He said: “They are each to be struck with thirty lashes, thirty lashes.” He said: But if he has done it? He said: “If it was short of penetration, then the hadd applies; and if he penetrated, he is made to stand, then struck one strike with the sword—the sword takes from him whatever it takes.” I said to him: Is that killing? He said: “That is so.”

I said: And regarding a woman who slept with another woman under one blanket? He said: “Is she one of forbidden kin?” I said: No. He said: “Is it out of necessity?” I said: No. He said: “They are each to be struck with thirty lashes, thirty lashes.”
I said: But she has done it. He said: That weighed heavily upon him, so he said: “Uff, uff, uff,” three times, and said: “The hadd.”

key_terms.الثَّقْبِ: penetration in the context of the act being discussed
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the prescribed legal punishment set by the Sacred Law
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ سَوْطًا: thirty lashes as a prescribed corporal punishment
key_terms.ذُو رَحِمٍ: a blood relative or kin relation
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity that may affect legal judgment
key_terms.مَحْرَمٍ: a person within prohibited degrees of marriageable kinship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhib al-Ahkam on two men or two women sleeping under one blanket and on liwat?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام concerning sleeping together under one blanket without kinship or necessity, and it then addresses the ruling when the prohibited act itself occurs. It distinguishes between lesser and more severe forms of the offense and states prescribed hadd punishments, reflecting the jurisprudential treatment of sexual transgressions in Shi'i legal tradition.
